question: Inside a single training example, why does a recurrent net have to step through positions one by one, and what gets worse as the sequence gets longer?
reply: A recurrent net must step through positions one by one because it generates a sequence of hidden states where each state depends on the previous hidden state and the current input, creating an inherently sequential nature that precludes parallelization within training examples [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 2, §1 Introduction]. As the sequence gets longer, the number of sequential operations required increases linearly to O(n), and the maximum path length between any two positions also increases to O(n), which makes learning long-range dependencies more difficult [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 6, §4 Why Self-Attention][Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 6].

question: Dot-product attention and additive attention have about the same theoretical cost. Why is scaled dot-product still preferred in practice, and why divide by √d_k when d_k is large?
reply: Scaled dot-product attention is preferred in practice because it is much faster and more space-efficient than additive attention, as it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4, §3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention]. The dot products are divided by $\sqrt{d_k}$ to counteract the effect of large $d_k$ values, which cause dot products to grow large in magnitude and push the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4, §3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention]. This scaling is necessary because, assuming independent random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, the dot product has a variance of $d_k$ [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4, §3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention].

question: dGSLM was already full-duplex. Which three limits does the paper still charge it with, and what does Moshi do differently?
reply: The paper charges dGSLM with three limitations: it does not run in an online fashion, it does not benefit from the knowledge of a text language model, and it does not model acoustic information as it only models semantic tokens [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6]. Moshi addresses these by modeling two streams of semantic and acoustic tokens hierarchically, allowing it to be full-duplex and exploit all available information [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6].
